review.summary:
No blocker. The artifact rebuilds to sha256 5bace6897a48b5b50e0f0815e966402bb6ba7ddf9b70286ee29aad71348dd84a in fresh copies of both the new and the pre-fix tree. The repository is unchanged, and the upload evidence (default params, no timeouts) is not affected by anything below.

I checked the fixes for R2-M1, R2-L1/BENCH-1 and R2-L2 through R2-L7 in the code and with probes. They do what they claim, with one exception: the JVM option variables are removed only when their names are upper case (R2-L4, F3).

- **Well-behaved process bots:** bench current vs boss (30 maps, threads 3, seedBase 100, turnMs 200) gives 60 of 60 per-game rows identical between the new and pre-fix trees. run submit vs v01 seed 5 gives 472 of 472 identical move lines.
- **Fresh seeds:** strict procCheck passes on seeds no one had used: boss 50@9000 gives 100/100, v01 50@8000 gives 100/100, 0 timeouts in both.
- **Mutations:** 25 of 45 one-edit mutations are caught and 20 survive (F4). The gaps are the Referee hand-off of extraLines, the env-variable removal, FileMerger.main's move-aside and cleanup, and the kills condition of the verdict.
- **Findings:**
  - Medium (F1): procCheck's printed rerun command leaves out -Pparams. Because procCheck rebuilds the artifact first, the rerun tests the default build instead of the one that failed, and project.md's timeout rule relies on that rerun.
  - Low (F2): after a long stall, the timeout note reads "0 line(s) arrived after the deadline ... no SLOW report". procCheck itself causes this by killing the artifact 500 ms after the game ends, yet the rule reads it as a machine stall.
  - Low: env removal misses mixed-case names on Windows (F3). A FileMerger test runs the real main() in the project directory and does not check that nothing changed (F5). A failed submit removes the rollback artifact (F6).

./gradlew --offline test in recheck4: 47/47 (BotFactory 3, Rules 20, ProcessBot 6, ProcessCheck 9, CGRunner 2, FileMerger 7).

Regression bench current vs boss (maps 30, threads 3, seedBase 100, turnMs 200), new vs pre-fix tree: all 60 per-game rows (seed, aSeat, winner, turns, score, errors) identical. Both 56/0/4, score 0.933. New tree: extraLines A=0 B=0 and every per-game extraLines is [0,0].
run -Pbot0=submit -Pbot1=v01 -Pseed=5 -Pprint=1 in both trees: 472 move lines identical, winner 0, 236 turns, 9:0. The new tree also prints extraLines=0/0.

Strict procCheck on fresh seeds in recheck4 (one job at a time). -Popp=boss -Pgames=50 -PseedBase=9000: exit 0, sameAsCurrent=100/100, timeouts=0, notCompared=0, extraLines=0, lateLines=0, stderrLines=0, minTurns=56, maxFirst=158.2ms. -Popp=v01 -Pgames=50 -PseedBase=8000: exit 0, 100/100, minTurns=42.

R2-M1 logic: an opponent's r.error is set only by rules.lastKill (timeout or invalid output) or by an in-process exception, which always leads to a kill. judge() checks both runs, and passed() needs same==total, so a game where the opponent was killed always fails. Mutations pc1-pc4 and pc12 are caught.
Turn numbers: finishKilled() increments s.turn, so 'killed on turn (turns-1)' is the 0-based turn of the kill and matches CGRunner's 'SLOW turn N'.

Extra lines: a well-behaved bot never has unread lines at send() or close(), so there are no false positives. Mini2 'pair5' (an extra WAIT/TRAIN pair on turn 5, so its answers lag one turn): the new run gives extraLines=0/2, and the bench JSON has per-seat [0,2]/[2,0], extraLinesB=12. The pre-fix tree dropped the pair silently.

R2-L3: ShimProbe (a hung direct DelayedEcho) closes in 528 ms and the bot JVM is dead afterwards. The process's descendants include conhost.exe, which is killed harmlessly. The wrapper test's mutations pb9 and pb13 are caught.

javapath shim: when a JVM runs ProcessBuilder("java", ...), the command resolves to the parent JDK's own bin first (info().command() = C:\Program Files\Java\jdk-17\bin\java.exe), so the shim is not the bot process under Gradle. The shim does start a child JVM (seen in the user's Serve process tree), and kill() would reach that child through descendants().

ATOMIC_MOVE of a directory on Windows: with Player.class held open even with FILE_SHARE_DELETE (probe Hold), FileMerger fails with 'AccessDeniedException: build\submit -> build\submit.old', the old artifact stays whole and no .old is left.
30 back-to-back FileMerger runs (java cr.submit.FileMerger ""): 0 failures, final sha 5bace689, no build/submit.old left.
ProcessBotTest (6 tests) under a 28-thread CPU burner on 14 logical CPUs: 2-3 loaded runs (22-24 s per class) and 3 more unloaded runs all passed.
close() when start() failed: proc stays null, so close() returns at once. Referee's finally then records extraLines=0 and the IOException still propagates.

findings.title: procCheck's rerun command omits -Pparams, so the 'quiet rerun' rebuilds and checks a different artifact
findings.evidence: ProcessCheck.java:48 prints "./gradlew procCheck " + quoted("-Popp=" + opp) + " -Pgames=1 -PseedBase=" + seed. procCheck dependsOn submit, and submit uses prop('params','') (build.gradle:63-68), so the printed command rebuilds the artifact with default params. project.md tells the user to reread a timeout-only failure without a SLOW report after a quiet rerun of the named seeds. Observed in recheck4: `./gradlew procCheck -Pparams=MAX_TOWERS=3 "-Popp=proc:java -version" -Pgames=1 -PseedBase=7` built sha256 f6fb382d42708df0... and printed `rerun: ./gradlew procCheck "-Popp=proc:java -version" -Pgames=1 -PseedBase=7`. Running that line verbatim rebuilt params="" sha256=5bace689... and checked that artifact instead. This does not affect the current upload, which uses default params.
findings.repro: In a copy: ./gradlew procCheck -Pparams=MAX_TOWERS=3 "-Popp=proc:java -version" -Pgames=1 -PseedBase=7 (the opponent times out, so the rerun line is printed). Paste the printed rerun line and compare the sha256 that submit prints in the two runs.
findings.suggested_fix: Add -Pparams=<the artifact's PARAMS> to the rerun line; ProcessCheck already reads them with artifactParams. Also print the artifact's sha256 in the summary so that a rerun can be matched to the build that failed.

findings.title: After a long stall the note reads '0 line(s) arrived after the deadline ... no SLOW report' because procCheck killed the artifact before it could report
findings.evidence: close() kills the program 500 ms after closing its input (ProcessBot.java:152), so a program still computing never prints its late answer or its SLOW line. judge() then writes 'no SLOW report' (ProcessCheck.java:101-104), which is the signature project.md reads as a delay outside the artifact's own turn. Variant recheck4/variants/e_late2000_turn5 (sleeps 2000 ms before answering on turn 5): procCheck -x submit -Popp=v01 -Pgames=1 printed 'killed on turn 5: Timeout; 0 line(s) arrived after the deadline; the artifact's own timing: no SLOW report' for both seats (lateLines=0, slowLines=0). Turn 0 has a related gap: the artifact's clock starts after the first token of the turn (InputReader.turnStartNanos). For seat 0 the referee's turn-0 window includes the JVM start, which the SLOW report never covers. This matches DEVLOG's 1001.2 ms turn-0 timeout 'with no SLOW report', which was read as a machine stall.
findings.repro: Put recheck4/variants/e_late2000_turn5/{Player.java,classes} into build/submit of a copy, then run ./gradlew procCheck -x submit -Popp=v01 -Pgames=1 -PseedBase=1.
findings.suggested_fix: Record in ProcessBot whether close() had to kill the program, and print 'killed before it answered or reported; no conclusion' in that case. For a program that timed out, wait longer before killing it. State in the note and in project.md that on turn 0 the SLOW report cannot cover JVM start or init.

findings.title: JVM option variables are removed only in upper case; on Windows a mixed-case name still reaches the bot and fails procCheck
findings.evidence: On Windows, ProcessBuilder.environment() is a case-sensitive HashMap (JDK 17 java.lang.ProcessEnvironment extends HashMap; remove() is super.remove), while the launcher and the JVM look the names up case-insensitively. ProcessBot.java:65 removes only the exact names. EnvProbe: with jdk_java_options or Java_Tool_Options set, the child's stderr is ['NOTE: Picked up JDK_JAVA_OPTIONS: -Xshare:auto'] or ['Picked up JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS: -Xshare:auto']. End to end on the pristine artifact: `env Java_Tool_Options=-Xshare:auto ./gradlew procCheck -x submit -Popp=v01 -Pgames=1 -PseedBase=1` exits 1 with stderrLines=2, while the upper-case JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS run exits 0.
findings.repro: In recheck4: env Java_Tool_Options=-Xshare:auto ./gradlew --offline -q procCheck -x submit -Popp=v01 -Pgames=1 -PseedBase=1. Or run probe.EnvProbe: java -cp 'probe/classes;build/classes/java/main' probe.EnvProbe build/classes/java/test with jdk_java_options set.
findings.suggested_fix: pb.environment().keySet().removeIf(k -> JVM_OPTION_VARS.stream().anyMatch(k::equalsIgnoreCase)), plus a unit test, which does not exist yet (see F4).

findings.title: 20 of 45 one-edit mutations survive the 47 tests
findings.evidence:
recheck4/mutate.log:
- Referee: the hand-off to Result.extraLines can be deleted (rf1), read before close() (rf2) or stored for the other seat (rf3), because no test drives Referee with a ProcessBot. run/bench extraLines and procCheck's extra-line check depend on it.
- ProcessBot: the JVM-variable removal can be dropped (pb11) or cut to one name (pb12). kill() can skip destroying the process itself (pb10), because no test closes a hung direct process. send() can sum instead of taking the max (pb2). A polled late line can go uncounted (pb5).
- ProcessCheck: Tally.passed can drop kills==0 (pc5, pc20) or timeouts==0 (pc6). kills==0 is the only guard when both runs are killed identically by the bot's own invalid command.
- FileMerger: a missing PARAMS marker can be accepted (fm3). removeOld can drop ATOMIC_MOVE (fm6), become plain deleteTree (fm7) or skip deleting a stale .old (fm9). A failed build can be left behind (fm8).
- Cosmetic: kill-note turn (pc14), minTurns (pc15), notCompared count (pc16), current-kill note (pc19).
findings.repro: python -I recheck4/scripts/mutate.py <copy> <log> [ids], using the Windows-style path (C:/...).
findings.suggested_fix: Add a Referee.play test with a DelayedEcho ProcessBot that checks Result.extraLines per seat. Add a ProcessBot test for env removal (child prints System.getenv) and for closing a hung direct process. Add a Tally test with kills=1, timeouts=0 and same=true. Add a FileMerger.main test with an injectable output directory: locked file, compile failure, stale .old, missing marker.

findings.title: FileMergerTest runs the real FileMerger.main in the project directory and does not check that 'nothing is touched'
findings.evidence: moreThanOneArgumentIsRejectedBeforeAnythingIsTouched (FileMergerTest.java:76-78) only checks that the exception is thrown. With the args check moved below removeOld, FileMergerTest still passes 7/7, but build/submit is deleted. With the check removed (fm4), the test fails, but running gradle test has already rewritten build/submit/Player.java with PARAMS = "MAX_TOWERS=3" (seen in recheck4/mut).
findings.repro: In a scratch copy with build/submit present, move the line 'if (args.length > 1) throw ...' to just after removeOld(outDir) and run ./gradlew test --rerun --tests cr.submit.FileMergerTest: it passes and build/submit is gone.
findings.suggested_fix: Compare the hash of build/submit before and after the call, or give main an output directory parameter and point the test at a @TempDir.

findings.title: Any failure after the move-aside leaves no build/submit/Player.java, the documented rollback artifact
findings.evidence: removeOld runs before the write and the compile (FileMerger.java:51-65). A merged-file compile error or a failed delete of build/submit.old ends with no artifact, as the Javadoc says. project.md, however, names build/submit/Player.java as the rollback artifact for 5bace689, whose sources are uncommitted. Repro in recheck4/mut: adding src/main/java/cr/core/Player.java ('public final class Player {}'), which compiles under Gradle, makes FileMerger fail with 'class Player is already defined', and build/submit is then gone.
findings.repro: Add that file in a copy and run java -cp build/classes/java/main cr.submit.FileMerger ""; build/submit no longer exists.
findings.suggested_fix: Compile into build/submit.new and swap it in only after the compile succeeds; keep build/submit.old until then. Alternatively keep a hashed copy of the rollback artifact outside build/.
